comment: Two of the nineteen inputs, the two beside the level shape knobs, carry no name in the maker's source and no printing on the panel; the manual's lettered diagram puts them under Level shape controls. Four of the thirty-four parameters have no widget on the panel: the clock pulses per beat, the HD switch and the anti-click switch, all three on the right-click menu. The buffer is a fixed 480000 samples, described in the source as 10 seconds at 48kHz, and the delay time is scaled against that figure rather than against the engine sample rate, which is the point the manual makes about 48000Hz. The DELAY knob is a linear ratio from -9 to +9: at or above zero the buffer is one plus the knob in seconds, and below zero it is one divided by one plus the knob, so the two ends are a tenth of a second and ten seconds. With a cable at CLOCK the same knob is rounded to a whole number and used as a multiplier or divider of the clocked length instead. The speed jacks are coloured as pitch rather than as a rate because they follow the volt-per-octave standard outright, which is what the manual says and what the module's use as an oscillator depends on. The reset input is read only in Phase beat mode (Igc.cpp:303-306).
